title: Senior's toolkit: fake clocks, test doubles and test runs
summary: TimeProvider, xUnit theories, NSubstitute, dotnet test filters and mutation testing with Stryker.NET.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: fake clocks, test doubles and test runs
steps.body: Testable design pays off only when the tests are quick to write and quick to run. These are the libraries and commands .NET teams use to control time, fake dependencies, run one test and check that the tests would catch a bug.

toolkit.what: The built-in clock abstraction (.NET 8+). Inject it instead of calling `DateTime.Now`, register `TimeProvider.System` in the app, and tests can control time.
flags: timers that a fake clock can fire
delays that a fake clock controls

toolkit.what: A clock you move by hand, from the package `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`. Time only passes when the test says so.
flags: move time forward; due timers fire
toolkit.example:
var clock = new FakeTimeProvider(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 3, 1, 9, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));
clock.Advance(TimeSpan.FromHours(25));

toolkit.what: xUnit's data-driven test: one test method, many rows of input and expected output. Edge cases become one line each.
flags: a single test with no parameters
rows from a static property, for complex objects
toolkit.example:
[Theory]
[InlineData(23, false)]
[InlineData(24, true)]
[InlineData(25, true)]
public void Due_after_24_hours(int hours, bool expected) { ... }

toolkit.what: NSubstitute, a widely used mocking library: create a fake of an interface, tell it what to return, check what was called.
flags: assert it was called exactly once with these arguments

toolkit.what: Run only the tests you care about, and see why they fail.
flags: names containing the text (`=` is exact, `!=` excludes)
print each test and its output
dump and stop a test that hangs

toolkit.what: Stryker.NET mutation testing: it changes your code (`>=` to `>`, `true` to `false`) and reruns the tests. A mutant that survives is a bug your tests would not catch.
flags: which project to mutate, when the test project references several
write an HTML report of surviving mutants
fail (for CI) when the mutation score is below 60%

steps.prompt: `SendsReminderAfter24Hours` passes on every laptop but fails in CI about one night in ten, always around midnight UTC. The code calls `DateTime.Now` and the test sleeps for a second. What is the fix?
options: Inject `TimeProvider`, and in the test use `FakeTimeProvider` with a fixed start and `Advance(TimeSpan.FromHours(24))`
Retry the test three times in CI
Increase the sleep to five seconds
steps.explain: A test that reads the real clock depends on when it runs. `UtcNow` removes the time-zone part but not the dependency. With a fake clock the test is exact, instant and the same at any hour.

steps.prompt: Match each NSubstitute call to what it does.
pairs: creates a fake that implements the interface

steps.prompt: The suite takes four minutes. Run only the tests in `ReminderTests`, and show each test's name and output.
steps.explain: `~` means contains, so it matches `Reminders.Tests.ReminderTests.SendsAfter24Hours`. `=` would need the full name. Detailed verbosity lists every test, not just the summary.

steps.prompt: Put the lines of a test for "the reminder is sent once after 24 hours" in order.
lines: var clock = new FakeTimeProvider(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 3, 1, 9, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));
also: var clock = new FakeTimeProvider(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 3, 1, 9, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));

steps.prompt: Stryker's report says: **Survived** `clock.GetUtcNow() >= at` mutated to `clock.GetUtcNow() > at`. What does that tell you?
options: No test checks the exact boundary: add a case where the time is exactly the due time
Stryker found a bug in production code; change `>=` to `>`
The test project does not compile
steps.explain: A surviving mutant means the tests pass whichever operator is used, so they never test the moment `now == at`. One `[InlineData(24, true)]` row kills it.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Anything that reads the clock, randomness or the network gets an injected seam (`TimeProvider`, an interface) on the day you write it. While working, run only your tests with `--filter`; before a big merge, run Stryker on the code you changed to see whether the tests would actually catch a mistake.
